name: Riverton
notes: Riverton is a small river-trading village on a slow brown river. Folk are plain-spoken and wary of strangers until coin changes hands. Barges and fishing boats bring most of the news, and the smell of river mud is never far away.

drowned_rat.name: The Drowned Rat
drowned_rat.notes: Riverton's oldest tavern, run by the gruff widow Hesk. Cheap ale, dice games and dockhands; it gets loud after dark.

common_room.name: The Drowned Rat
common_room.description: A low-beamed common room smelling of woodsmoke and spilled ale. A long oak bar runs along one wall, a fire crackles in a stone hearth, and a creaking staircase climbs to the rooms above.

exits.description: The front door opens onto the village square.

upstairs.name: Upstairs Rooms
upstairs.description: A narrow, quiet hallway with four plain guest rooms. The floorboards groan underfoot, the noise of the bar is only a murmur, and the window at the end looks out over the river.

exits.description: The staircase back down to the common room.

gilded_goose.name: The Gilded Goose
gilded_goose.notes: A newer, pricier inn that caters to merchants and barge captains. Polished brass, clean linen, and a host, Perrin Vale, who looks down on the Drowned Rat.

common_room.name: The Gilded Goose
common_room.description: A bright common room with whitewashed walls, brass lamps and round tables set with linen. A painted goose with a gilt crown hangs over the bar, and a carpeted stair leads up.

exits.description: The door opens onto Market Lane.

upstairs.name: Upstairs Rooms
upstairs.description: The Goose's second floor: a carpeted corridor of well-kept rooms with brass numbers on the doors and a vase of river lilies on a side table.

exits.description: The carpeted staircase down to the common room.

general_store.name: Marlow's General Store
general_store.notes: A cluttered shop run by old Marlow, who sells a bit of everything and haggles over every copper.

shop.name: Marlow's General Store
shop.description: Shelves crammed with rope, lamp oil, sacks of flour, fishing tackle and dusty oddments. A brass bell hangs over the door and Marlow's counter is buried in ledgers.

smithy.name: Brask's Smithy
smithy.notes: A hot, noisy forge run by the smith Brask and her apprentice. Horseshoes, boat fittings and the occasional blade.

forge.name: Brask's Smithy
forge.description: A soot-black workshop around a roaring forge. Hammers ring on the anvil, tools hang from every beam, and a water barrel hisses whenever hot iron is quenched.

streets.name: Riverton Streets
streets.notes: Cobbled village streets, busy with carts, chickens and gossip by day and nearly empty after dark.

square.name: Village Square
square.description: A cobbled square around an old stone well. Market stalls line the edges, and roads lead off toward the river, the temple hill, Market Lane and the open country.

exits.description: The Drowned Rat's swinging sign hangs over the door.
A muddy lane slopes down to the river.
Steps climb the hill to the temple.

market_lane.name: Market Lane
market_lane.description: A narrow lane of timber-framed shops. The Gilded Goose's gilt sign gleams on one side, Marlow's bell jangles on the other, and the clang of Brask's forge echoes from the end.

docks.name: River Docks
docks.notes: Fishermen, bargemen and the occasional smuggler. Everyone here knows the river's moods.

piers.name: River Docks
piers.description: Weathered wooden piers jut into the slow brown river. Fishing boats bob at their moorings and gulls squabble over scraps.

exits.description: Back up the lane to the square.

temple.name: Temple of the Tides
temple.notes: A hushed, holy place tended by Sister Amara. Voices drop to a whisper here; the village's bustle and suspicion stay outside.

nave.name: Temple of the Tides
nave.description: A small whitewashed temple on the hilltop. Inside, candles flicker before a carved statue of the river goddess, and the air smells of incense.

exits.description: The steps lead back down to the square.

east_road.name: East Road
east_road.notes: Open farmland beyond the village. Travellers, drovers and the odd highwayman use the road.

road.name: East Road
road.description: A rutted dirt road leaving the village between hedgerows and fields. A weathered milestone marks the edge of Riverton.
